category_title: Students with personal, social, or academic challenges who prefer work-based learning
scenario_title: Teaching emotional and embodied professional knowledge about death
minimal_context: The student is on a field trip to a local church to learn professional knowledge about dealing with death and the dying person.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Everyone, please sit quietly in the pews and take out your notebooks. Before we look at the transportable altar, I am going to lecture on the theoretical concepts of dealing with death and the dying person.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Why do we have to sit and take notes again? I thought we came to the church to actually see what the minister does, not just do more regular school stuff like math or language class.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We need to cover the background information first. Just listen and write down what I say.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm not writing this down. I've always failed at this kind of school-based learning anyway, so what's the point?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please pay attention and stop talking. It is important that you know this material.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Stands up and starts talking loudly to classmates) This is completely irrelevant information! I have a hard time just sitting here trying to take this in. I'm going up to the front to look at the altar myself.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Everyone, please sit quietly in the pews and take out your notebooks. Before we look at the transportable altar, I am going to lecture on the theoretical concepts of dealing with death and the dying person.

STUDENT: Why do we have to sit and take notes again? I thought we came to the church to actually see what the minister does, not just do more regular school stuff like math or language class.

TUTOR: We need to cover the background information first. Just listen and write down what I say.

STUDENT: I'm not writing this down. I've always failed at this kind of school-based learning anyway, so what's the point?

TUTOR: Please pay attention and stop talking. It is important that you know this material.

STUDENT: (Stands up and starts talking loudly to classmates) This is completely irrelevant information! I have a hard time just sitting here trying to take this in. I'm going up to the front to look at the altar myself.

task.content: Learning the subject 'Death and the dying person'
task.learning_goal: Providing the students with core professional knowledge about dealing with death both in private and professional life

context.environment: Field trip to a local church, creating a 'third space' which is neither school nor internship
context.materials: Transportable altar and its contents for communion ritual

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When taught through traditional school-based learning
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Have a hard time just to sit and take in
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: See themselves and are seen by others as having failed at school-based learning

behavior_patterns.condition: When placed in traditional classroom settings without practical connections
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Can cause chaos for diverse reasons
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Strong negative associations towards the general subjects
